key_concepts: Motion can be described using distance and time
Speed is the distance traveled divided by the time of travel
Speed can be calculated using the formula speed = distance ÷ time
Speed can be expressed in meters per second (m/s)
Speed can be expressed in kilometers per hour (km/h)
A faster object covers a given distance in less time
A race winner is determined by the shortest travel time for the same distance
Distance can be measured using a meter stick, ruler, or measuring tape
Time can be measured using a stopwatch or timer
Accurate measurements are important when describing motion
Factors such as added weight or changed wheels can affect a toy car's speed
Walking slower increases travel time while walking faster decreases travel time
